atomicity.reason: One obligation - publish one fallback limit on one timeout of one actuator interface; the cooling and heating triggers are the same failure mode on the same actuator.

comprehensibility.reason: Intelligible on its own - it names the trigger, the timeout, the published value and the reason for capping power.

feasibility.reason: Feasible, but it publishes a second permitted discharge power alongside REQ_POWER_DERATING's characteristic with no precedence rule, so between 55 C and 60 C two requirements demand different values on the same interface (derating gives about 40 % at 58 C against this requirement's 30 %).
feasibility.suggestion: Define a single publishing rule shared by both requirements - e.g. the published permitted discharge power is the minimum of every applicable limit - so the two cannot disagree.

parent_fit.reason: Serves the parent story's promise of a reduced but predictable power level rather than a cut-out, extending it to the case where the pack can no longer influence its own temperature.

unambiguity.reason: Two readings for what appears on the interface: the 30 % fallback could replace the thermal derating value or be combined with it, and the requirement does not say. It is also open whether the fallback is released when a confirmation finally arrives.
unambiguity.suggestion: State the arbitration (e.g. the published limit is the minimum of all applicable limits) and the condition under which the fallback is withdrawn.

verifiability.reason: The 2 s timeout is concrete, but 'confirmed by the coolant actuator' names no confirmation signal or acceptance criterion, and '30 % of the full permitted discharge power' rests on a quantity that is defined nowhere, so the expected published value cannot be computed for a test.
verifiability.suggestion: Name the confirmation signal and what counts as a confirmation, and quantify the full permitted discharge power that the 30 % refers to.

summary: Sound failsafe intent, but it publishes a second permitted discharge power on the same interface as REQ_POWER_DERATING with no arbitration rule, and neither 'confirmed' nor 'full permitted discharge power' is defined.
